verdict.rationale: LiteLLM publishes a formal API Stability Policy that defines the proxy's public surface. Every deployed proxy serves a generated OpenAPI spec at /openapi.json and a Swagger UI at its root, and a semver/release-cycle contract backs this up. It also exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints plus REST endpoints such as /mcp-rest/tools/call that can be driven with curl. missing for 10: a vendor-hosted public spec download (the probe found no hosted openapi.json; the spec exists only on user-deployed proxies), independent hands-on corroboration of the admin/management API endpoints.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Every endpoint that appears in the proxy's OpenAPI spec is public
The spec is served at `/openapi.json` and rendered as Swagger UI at `/` by default
Your Proxy Swagger is available on the root of the Proxy: e.g.: `http://localhost:4000/`
call tools with curl without an LLM
